references.text: The same instruction to take the fat that covers the entrails, the large lobe of the liver, both kidneys, and the fat on them, given in the context of the peace offering.
Parallel description of the fat, the lobe of the liver, and the kidneys to be offered with a peace offering from the flock.
The same sacrificial parts mentioned for the peace offering of a goat: the fat that covers the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver.
For the sin offering, the same parts are to be taken: the fat, the lobe of the liver, and the kidneys, and burned on the altar.
For the guilt offering, the same fatty parts are mentioned: the fat, the tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver.
Moses carries out the instruction from Exodus 29:13 at the consecration of the tabernacle, taking the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys.
At the consecration offering, Moses takes the fat, the tail, all the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys.
Aaron burns the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering on the altar, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The fatty parts from the bull and the ram, including the tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver, are placed on the altar.
Describes the second part of the same consecration ritual with identical specifications.
